- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward correction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overcorrects downward — cap forecast decline to 10–15% of prior peak.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of history.  
- If forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong upward momentum, reduce forecast ceiling by 5–10% to avoid horizon overestimation.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.1) and forecast is trending, apply slight smoothing — avoid abrupt changes unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive sentiment spikes.
